rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body (lines 55-56) names the dominant failure mode — Claude dumping all four screening criteria across all three bug candidates at once — and the actual recovery move is a paste-ready fenced prompt (lines 60-64: 'Use the AskUserQuestion tool for speeding up screening and making suggestions. One candidate at a time.'), not a free-form chat instruction. Matches check_prompts.md §15(b)'s sanctioned 'body callout right after fence, hands student choice' shape. Soft, non-blocking note: the PRIMARY bug-screen prompt doesn't itself structurally force one-at-a-time pacing beyond 'ask one question at a time if you need to' — the discipline is enacted via the conditional escape hatch, which is a legitimate two-tier design, not a defect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body teaches the work; trainer manages the room outside text.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.

'One decision, and you probably have a strong candidate already' (line 21) respects the self-taught engineer's existing competence rather than framing the step as remediation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity — consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, mood-doesn't-resolve-early.

Bring a moment Claude Code frustrated you.') matches M1's actual Connections opener verbatim (getting-going.md line 21: 'The question (to you): what's one trick you figured out with Claude Code that nobody taught you?'). You find them.', line 64) — consonant with the strategy doc's 'never sold as a gap-fix' / wizard-status positioning. Mood doesn't resolve early: the bug is picked, not fixed; nothing here pre-empts M1's teaching moment.
